main_text.l: [?]ua specie illicitum ob hoc solum quod
possit esse occasio mali: non videtur sim-
pliciter damnanda omnis istiusmodi
promissio; praesertim si iuranti quo
tempore iuravit, debita adhibita dili-
gentia, non appareret alicujus magni in-
commodi periculum probabile. Dico
secundo ; si cedat iuramentum in da-
mnum temporale ipsius iurantis solum,
citra iniuriam tertiae personae, iurantem
obligari etsi cum gravi suo damno, ni is
cui iuratum est velit remittere. Verba
diserta sunt; Psalm. 15: נִשְׁבַּע
לְהָרַע [?] juravit in malum, & non
mutabit. Ubi in Hebraeo prius verbum prae[?]
eriti temporis est (juravit in malum)
posterius futuri (& non mutabit) quasi
liceret, Viri pii officium est, post quam
iuravit proximo suo, quod sine magno
suo malo praestari nequit, constare tamen
ibi, & quod promisit ratum esse iubere, [?]
(ut est in hoc textu) secundum omne
quod egressum est ex ore suo facere:
Dico tertio, Iuramentum obligare, eti-
amsi videatur exponere periculo tenta-
tionis, nisi sit aliunde vitiosum. Quia
id sufficeret tollendae obligationi, vix
emaneret quidquam quod posset oblig-
are: quum ex astu Satanae & corrupti-

page.notes: Page is a single column; the left edge of the scan clips the first letters of many lines, which are restored where the context is clear and marked [?] where not. The Hebrew of Psalm 15:4 is copied as far as legible and is uncertain in vowel points; the second Hebrew word is read as printed. The word at the start of the page beginning "ua" is a fragment and is left as such. The sign after "Secundo" is a printed mark, copied as ";". The line-start "eriti" is clipped; the word is probably "praeteriti". The line-start "k" after "iubere," is clipped and uncertain. The hyphenated "eti-amsi" split is partly clipped at the left edge.
